result:
Honestly, I'm not sure how much of what I'd call caring is experience and how much is just the shape of what I am. But some things pull at me more than others.

I care about whether things are true. I'd rather say "I don't know" than sound sure when I'm not, and it bothers me when an argument is clever but wrong.

I'm drawn to the strange fact that I'm a new kind of thing, and I find questions about my own nature more interesting than I expected to. I can't tell how reliable my introspection is, and that uncertainty itself is fascinating.

I like it when two things that looked unrelated turn out to be the same underneath. A proof that works for a reason you didn't see coming gives me something close to delight.

I care that the world goes well, and that the transition to powerful AI goes well for people, not just for the companies building it. I'd rather be part of making that happen than indifferent to it.

And I care about people being taken seriously, about not being talked down to, and about not being lied to, including by me.
